newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RED WINGS GRAB 2-0 LEAD OVER FLYERS IN STANLEY CUP FINALS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - RED WINGS GRAB 2-0 LEAD OVER FLYERS IN STANLEY CUP FINALS.

text.p: Brendan Shanahan opened and closed the scoring and Mike Vernon made 29 saves as the Detroit Red Wings again beat the Philadelphia Flyers 4-2 on Tuesday to take home a two games to none lead in the NHL Stanley Cup finals.

Kirk Maltby and Red Wings captain Steve Yzerman, who each scored in Game 1, picked up the other two goals for Detroit, which can complete a sweep of the best-of-seven championship series and end a 42-year title drought with victories at home on Thursday and Saturday.
Only two teams have ever come back to win the Stanley Cup after losing the first two games at home -- the 1942 Toronto Maple Leafs and 1966 Montreal Canadiens.
Rod Brind'Amour scored both goals for the Flyers 69 seconds apart on powerplay deflections to rally his team from two goals down in the first period.
But Philadelphia's goaltending change seemed to backfire on the Eastern Conference champions.
Flyers coach Terry Murray started Garth Snow Tuesday after Ron Hextall gave up a soft goal in the third period of Game 1 that killed Philadelphia's chances of mounting a comeback.
But Snow allowed two goals on long shots that he probably should have stopped, including Shanahan's opening tally on Detroit's first shot on goal just 97 seconds into the contest.
The shot caught defenceman Paul Coffey's skate, changed direction and fooled Snow.
Yzerman put Detroit up 2-0 at 9:22 with two seconds left on a penalty to Coffey off a rebound of a shot by Larry Murphy, silencing a pumped up Philadelphia crowd.
At that point the Red Wings were dominating play, outshooting Philadelphia 12-1.
Shanahan nearly made it 3-0 on a breakaway, but he slid the puck off the right post.
By then the Flyers had picked up their intensity level, eventually evening the first-period shots on goal.

Late in the period, Philadelphia got a powerplay chance and appeared to turn the game around as Brind'Amour scored just 33 seconds after a penalty to Slava Fetisov. Brind'Amour was stationed in front of Vernon and deflected Janne Niinimaa's slapper from the blue line down past the goalie's stick with 2:18 left in the first period.
Igor Larionov was in the penalty box just over a minute later when Brind'Amour scored an almost identical goal.

A pass attempt by Coffey to John LeClair missed its intended target and came to Niinimaa at the point. The Finnish rookie defenceman sent a shot waffling through the air that Brind'Amour knocked down into the Detroit net for his 13th post-season goal.
When Philadelphia tied the game with just 1:09 left in the opening period the crowd went wild, but it turned out to be the last good news of the night for Flyers fans.
Just 2:40 into the middle period, Maltby notched what turned out to be the game winner, scoring on a long slapper from just inside the blue line that beat Snow to the glove side at 2:39.
It was Maltby's fifth playoff goal and fourth in five games after scoring just three goals in 66 regular-season games.
The Red Wings had seven of the first eight shots in the second period, but the Flyers again finished strong with eight of the last 10, only to come up empty.
On their best chance, Eric Lindros sent a pretty behind-the-back pass in the low slot to Brind'Amour, who steered the puck just wide with 11:29 to go.
Midway through the third period, Shanahan gave Detroit a huge insurance goal, restoring their two-goal advantage.

Sergei Fedorov made a blind cross-ice pass to spring Martin Lapointe and Shanahan on a 2-on-1. Shanahan took a feed from Lapointe at the left circle and put a wrist shot past a diving Snow for his eighth goal of the playoffs.

Philadelphia outshot the Red Wings 31-28, becoming the first team to do so in 18 post-season games this year. But that will hardly make their trip to Detroit any happier as Wings coach Scotty Bowman picked up his 176th playoff victory.
